chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:

I was in Al-Madina during the month of Ramadan, so I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I intend to perform Itikaaf, so what should I say and what should I impose upon myself?' He said, 'Do not go out of the mosque except for a need that is indispensable, and do not sit under the shades until you return to your seat.'

key_terms.أَعْتَكِفَ: I intend to perform Itikaaf (spiritual retreat)
key_terms.لِحَاجَةٍ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهَا: For a need that is indispensable/inevitable

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for leaving the mosque during Itikaaf?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the boundaries of Itikaaf by emphasizing strict adherence to the mosque premises, prohibiting unnecessary exits and discouraging movement to different shaded areas to maintain spiritual focus. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on minimizing worldly distractions during the retreat, ensuring the worshipper remains in a state of continuous devotion within the sacred space.
